newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India to become jet fuel exporter by 1999.
newsitem.headline: India to become jet fuel exporter by 1999.

text.p: An explosion of new refineries in India towards the end of the century will turn the country into a jet fuel exporter, an industry official said on Wednesday.

"Jet fuel production from Indian refineries is more or less in line with demand except for a minor shortfall up to the year 1997-98," said A.K.Bansal, General Manager (Aviation) of Bharat Petroleum Corp
"Thereafter, there is considerable surplus which will need to be exported."
He said the surplus would be 920,000 tonnes in the 1998-99 year ending March due to the startup of several new refineries during this period.

Among these are Reliance Petroleum's 300,000-barrel-per-day refinery near the port of Jannagar on India's west coast, Indian Oil Corp's (IOC) 120,000-bpd unit in Panipat in the northern state of Haryana state.
Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals (MRPL) will raise capacity by 120,000-bpd to 180,000-bpd at its refinery in the country's west coast of Magalore.
Three other smaller refineries with an average refining capacity of 60,000-bpd are also due up during this period.
Bansal said although India would have to export jet fuel, it would continue to import kerosene, used for lighting, heating and cooking.
Indian jet fuel demand for the next four years will grow at an average rate of about 7 percent per annum, Bansal said.
The projected growth, he said, was due to "globalisation/liberalisation of the Indian economy," which has boosted passenger and cargo traffic.
Bansal said international passenger traffic for 1995-96 grew by 19.94 percent to 10.67 million while cargo traffic grew by 15.62 percent to 433,211 tonnes, both over the previous 1994-95 year.

To meet the rising demand, India is getting the private sector to build four new international airports at Cochin, Bangalore, Goa and Bombay. Construction of the Cochin airport has already started, Bansal said.

He said that although parts of the Indian oil market had been liberalised, jet fuel deregulation was not expected until 2000. India has already liberalised the imports of liquified petroleum gas, kerosene and lubricants.
